levelNote: Foundational UGC NET English Literature MCQs on Restoration drama, Dryden, Pope, Swift, Addison, Steele, Defoe, Richardson, Fielding, Sterne, Johnson, Gray and Goldsmith.

questions.question: Which year marks the reopening of English public theatres after the Interregnum?
questions.explanation: The Restoration of Charles II in 1660 brought the return of licensed public theatre.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which dramatic genre is especially associated with fashionable wit and sexual intrigue on the Restoration stage?
questions.explanation: Restoration comedy of manners satirizes fashionable behaviour, courtship and social hypocrisy.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote The Way of the World (1700)?
questions.explanation: Congreve wrote The Way of the World, a landmark comedy of manners.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which pioneering woman dramatist wrote The Rover?
questions.explanation: Aphra Behn wrote The Rover, first performed in 1677.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which change distinguished the English professional stage after 1660?
options: Plays could only be performed in Latin
questions.explanation: Women entered the professional public stage in the Restoration, unlike the earlier all-male companies.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who became Poet Laureate in 1668?
questions.explanation: Dryden received the office of Poet Laureate in 1668.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which Dryden poem satirizes the Exclusion Crisis through a biblical allegory?
questions.explanation: Absalom and Achitophel (1681) uses the story of David and Absalom to address contemporary politics.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Dryden’s All for Love reworks the story of which lovers?
questions.explanation: All for Love (1677) is Dryden’s tragedy about Antony and Cleopatra.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which work is Dryden’s famous dialogue on dramatic criticism?
questions.explanation: An Essay of Dramatic Poesy (1668) debates principles of drama through four speakers.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What verse form did Dryden notably refine for satire and argument?
questions.explanation: Dryden became a leading master of rhymed iambic-pentameter couplets.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote The Rape of the Lock?
questions.explanation: Alexander Pope created the mock-heroic poem The Rape of the Lock.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What object is cut from Belinda in The Rape of the Lock?
questions.explanation: The Baron cuts a lock of Belinda’s hair, producing the poem’s mock-epic conflict.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote An Essay on Man?
questions.explanation: Pope’s philosophical poem An Essay on Man appeared in epistles during 1733–34.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: The Dunciad principally attacks what?
questions.explanation: Pope’s satirical epic presents the triumph of Dulness.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which verse form is strongly associated with Pope’s major poems?
questions.explanation: Pope’s polished rhyming pentameter couplets became emblematic of Augustan verse.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote Gulliver’s Travels?
questions.explanation: Jonathan Swift published Gulliver’s Travels in 1726.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What are the tiny inhabitants encountered in Gulliver’s first voyage called?
questions.explanation: Lilliput is the country of miniature people in Part I of Gulliver’s Travels.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which Swift prose satire proposes an outrageous solution to Irish poverty?
questions.explanation: A Modest Proposal (1729) uses shocking irony to criticize exploitation and indifference.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which creatures embody rational horses in Gulliver’s Travels?
questions.explanation: The Houyhnhnms are the rational horses of the fourth voyage.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which periodical was founded by Richard Steele in 1709?
questions.explanation: Steele launched The Tatler in 1709 under the persona Isaac Bickerstaff.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which periodical did Addison and Steele establish in 1711?
questions.explanation: The Spectator began in 1711 and helped popularize the periodical essay.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote the tragedy Cato (1713)?
questions.explanation: Joseph Addison’s Cato is a neoclassical tragedy first produced in 1713.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who created the fictional journalist Isaac Bickerstaff for The Tatler?
questions.explanation: Steele used the Bickerstaff persona in the early issues of The Tatler.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote Robinson Crusoe?
questions.explanation: Daniel Defoe published Robinson Crusoe in 1719.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What is the name of Crusoe’s companion whom he rescues?
questions.explanation: Crusoe names the rescued man Friday.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which Defoe novel follows a woman through crime, survival and repentance?
questions.explanation: Moll Flanders (1722) follows its resourceful heroine through a turbulent life.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which Defoe work presents a fictionalized account of London’s plague?
options: A Journal of the Plague Year
questions.explanation: Defoe published A Journal of the Plague Year in 1722, depicting the 1665 outbreak.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote Pamela; or, Virtue Rewarded?
questions.explanation: Richardson published Pamela in 1740.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What form is central to Samuel Richardson’s major novels?
questions.explanation: Richardson narrates through letters, presenting characters’ experiences and emotions directly.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What is the surname of Clarissa, heroine of Richardson’s novel?
questions.explanation: Clarissa Harlowe is the central character of Richardson’s Clarissa.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What is the chief concern of Pamela?
options: A servant woman’s virtue and social position
questions.explanation: Pamela centres on a young servant resisting her employer’s advances and questions of virtue and class.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling?
questions.explanation: Fielding’s Tom Jones was published in 1749.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who is the author of Joseph Andrews?
questions.explanation: Henry Fielding published Joseph Andrews in 1742.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What is the title of Fielding’s parody of Richardson’s Pamela?
questions.explanation: Fielding’s An Apology for the Life of Mrs Shamela Andrews (1741) satirizes Pamela.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which heroine is Tom Jones’s principal beloved?
questions.explanation: Sophia Western is the central love interest in Tom Jones.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman?
questions.explanation: Laurence Sterne’s Tristram Shandy appeared in nine volumes between 1759 and 1767.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which novel by Sterne features the traveller Yorick?
questions.explanation: Yorick narrates Sterne’s A Sentimental Journey Through France and Italy (1768).
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which device is especially associated with Tristram Shandy?
questions.explanation: Sterne’s novel playfully digresses and experiments with its printed form.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: In which year did Samuel Johnson publish his Dictionary of the English Language?
questions.explanation: Johnson’s Dictionary of the English Language appeared in 1755.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which periodical essay series did Johnson begin in 1750?
questions.explanation: Johnson’s Rambler essays were published from 1750 to 1752.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote Rasselas?
questions.explanation: Samuel Johnson published Rasselas in 1759.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who compiled Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets?
questions.explanation: Johnson’s Lives of the Poets appeared between 1779 and 1781.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which critic wrote the Preface to Shakespeare in 1765?
questions.explanation: Johnson’s 1765 edition of Shakespeare included his influential Preface.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard?
questions.explanation: Thomas Gray published his famous Elegy in 1751.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What setting is evoked by Gray’s Elegy?
questions.explanation: The poem opens at twilight in a country churchyard.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Thomas Gray is commonly associated with which pre-Romantic group?
questions.explanation: Gray’s reflective poetry is often discussed in the tradition of the Graveyard poets.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote She Stoops to Conquer?
questions.explanation: Goldsmith’s comedy She Stoops to Conquer was staged in 1773.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who wrote The Vicar of Wakefield?
questions.explanation: Goldsmith published The Vicar of Wakefield in 1766.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which Goldsmith poem laments the decline of rural community?
questions.explanation: Goldsmith’s The Deserted Village (1770) contrasts rural happiness with displacement and depopulation.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which character is the central young woman of She Stoops to Conquer?
questions.explanation: Kate Hardcastle pretends to be a barmaid to overcome Marlow’s shyness.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ
